data.long_meaning: In Greek, Filippa derives from Philippos, meaning 'friend of horses'. The name has a rich history in both the Greek and Christian traditions, and was borne by several early Christian saints. The name Filippa carries the meaning “Lover of horses” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Filippa usually hope their child will grow to embody lover of horses and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Filippa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Φιλιππα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φιλιππα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις φίλος που σημαίνει αγάπη και ίππος που σημαίνει άλογο, επομένως το όνομα σημαίνει αυτή που αγαπάει τα άλογα, είναι ένα όνομα με ιστορία στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας και συνδέεται με χαρακτηριστικά όπως η δύναμη και το θάρρος

in_latin.name: Filippa

in_english.name: Filippa

data.cultural_impact: Filippa was a common name during the Roman Empire, particularly among the noble and affluent classes due to its royal and aristocratic origins. The name continued to be popular throughout Europe, particularly in the Middle Ages, and was believed to bring good fortune and honor.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Filippa is the name of several notable saints. Saint Filippa of Ducea was a brave widow and mother, who offered her child as a sacrifice to save her village from an invading army. Another Saint Filippa, also known as Saint Filippa of Nero, was a Roman virgin and martyr who was tortured and beheaded during the persecution of Christians during the reign of Emperor Nero. The name Filippa is often associated with strong faith, perseverance in the face of adversity, and deep spirituality. It is a reminder of the power of faith to transform even the darkest moments of our lives into opportunities for growth and sanctity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Filippa: Derived from Filippos in Greek, meaning "lover of horses" or "horse-loving." In a spiritual context, this name may symbolize a deep connection to the natural world and its creatures, or a passionate and free spirit.

historical_references.reference: Filippa of Swabia (1172-1231) was an influential queen consort of Germany and Bohemia. She was the elder daughter of the Duke of Swabia and married Emperor Otto IV in 1209.
historical_references.context: Filippa played a significant role in the Investiture Controversy between the Church and the Emperor, supporting Emperor Otto IV against Pope Innocent III.

historical_references.reference: Filippa of Hainault (1292-1369) was a Flemish noblewoman who became queen consort of England in 1328 upon her marriage to King Edward III.
historical_references.context: Filippa was instrumental in promoting the causes of her husband during the Hundred Years War between England and France. She played a role in the education of her sons, the future kings Edward the Black Prince and Richard II.
